sources.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming Israel government
Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming Israel government

en.title: Netanyahu and Eisenkot parties conclude coalition talks without agreement
en.dek: Negotiations between Benjamin Netanyahu's and Gadi Eisenkot's parties ended on 23 November without forming a coalition.
facts: Netanyahu and Eisenkot parties concluded coalition talks on 23 November 2026 without reaching an agreement
Both sides stated they outlined their positions on substantive issues and discussed them in detail
The talks aimed to form an Israel government following recent elections
No deal was reached despite detailed discussions on key issues
Both parties confirmed the conclusion of negotiations without a coalition pact
The outcome leaves the process of government formation ongoing
body: Netanyahu and Eisenkot parties concluded coalition talks on 23 November without reaching a deal, according to The Hindu and The Japan Times.
Both sides stated they outlined their positions on substantive issues and discussed them in detail, as reported by The Hindu.
The negotiations were part of ongoing efforts to form an Israel government following recent electoral results.
Neither party issued a joint statement confirming cooperation, with both confirming the talks ended without agreement.
The conclusion of talks means the process of forming a coalition government remains unresolved.
Political analysts noted the significance of the breakdown between the two party factions.
en.context: Coalition talks are a standard part of Israel's parliamentary system following elections, requiring parties to negotiate agreements to secure a majority in the Knesset. The involvement of Netanyahu's faction and Eisenkot's party represents a notable alignment in the current political landscape.
